title: A shopping mall/leisure centre complex with staff hallways and a hidden abandoned room that leads to labyrinths and tunnels.
content: I have no idea if this post is relevant to the sub or other people's experiences, but I thought I'd share my most common reccuring dreams. Edit - leisure centre for Americans is a Sports centre, or somewhere with swimming pools and gyms where you can play sports. Dunno what you guys call it. A few years ago I kept having dreams that I was in a big building, and it was always different in each dream. Sometimes a mall, or a hotel, sometimes a leisure centre with a massive pool and slides, sometimes a complex that had a cinema and a bowling alley. The thing that was always the same was that I worked there, and I was looking after a big group, sometimes just children but sometimes adults too. The common theme was always that I was rushed off my ass, and there would be an emergency or something similar that cause me to go through loads of doors that were like staff doors, or back alleys to the big building I was in. I'll come back to this dream in a second, but I briefly need to tell you about another set of reccuring dreams I had. Probably about 10 years ago I felt pretty lost in life, and for quite a while I had constant dreams about labyrinths. In the dreams, common places from my waking life would have entrances to an underground labyrinth. I remember there was an entrance in the playground of my first school, one in the graveyard next to that school, one near a house I lived in when I was a kid, and a few others. For a while in these dreams I would be very afraid of these labyrinth entrances. They were like big crypt doors that you would heave open, and the walls were lined with torches. Once I managed to get the courage to go into a labyrinth I would spend hours walking them, and I knew there were ghosts or spirits down there that I wouldn't want to find me, and eventually I would find an exit that was at another prominent place of my childhood. I gradually got more comfortable going into the labyrinths, and spent so much time down there I felt like I could map them in my dream. I never came across the ghosts, but I knew they aren't good. Back to the mall/hotel/big building dreams. I remember one prominent dream where I was in a leisure centre/cinema/hotel, like all of the locations combined, looking after loads of kids, and rushing around all the staff doors. I remember the view out of these big windows was a harbour with boats. I opened a staff door and was suddenly in an enormous red brick room, that had been abandoned for a long time. There was rubble on the floor, and high windows on the left hand side with sunlight coming through, so you could see all the motes of dust in the sunlight beams. On the right side of the room were three doors that were all shut. On the other side of the room was a stone staircase to another door, which I knew would take me back to the swimming pool/cinema/hotel/whatever building I worked in. There were a few ghosts (the same ones from the labyrinth dreams) floating around the room, and I knew they couldn't see me. I knew I had to traverse the room, avoiding the rubble and ghosts to get to the other door, and I knew I couldn't touch any of the ghosts. I had almost made it to the stairs on the other side and the middle door out of the three on the right slammed open, and something was coming out of it to get me (I couldn't see what was coming, I could just feel the energy of something rushing toward the door). I then realised that behind the three doors were the labyrinths from my recurring dreams years before. I ran the fuck up the stairs and through the door, back to work and back to the odd rush of being busy and looking after the group I was monitoring. I think I woke up shortly after. The odd thing is I never dreamt of the labyrinths or the shopping mall/hotel place again. Sorry, very long. I had to get that out as these posts and this phenomena remind me of that place in my dreams so much, and those dreams have stuck with me for such a long time.
